title: Gangnam Café
description:
{name} orders a 6,500 won americano.
Just once, {name} wants to sit in a Gangnam café
where people talk about sums far beyond the price of coffee.

Next table. A man in a suit, on a call.
"That's the last right to a new unit in the redevelopment. If you don't lock it in today, it's gone.
Redevelopment's confirmed. ...Yes, 50 million won in cash is enough."

{name}'s ear drifts over on its own.

choices.result_text: He does not notice. The numbers lodge themselves one by one in {name}'s head.

choices.text: Tune it out. Focus on the resume.
choices.result_text: {name} fills in the blanks on his résumé, but the voices at the next table keep catching his ear.

choices.text: The seat is uncomfortable. Just leave.
choices.result_text:
{name} gets up and leaves the cold coffee behind.
When the café door closes, the voice at the next table cuts off.

title: The Gap
description:
The man hangs up and stands. Bathroom, maybe.
His phone and — a document folder, left on the table.
Bold text on the cover: "XX District Housing Association Allocation Guide."

Nobody around is paying attention.
{name}'s heart quickens slightly.

choices.text: Flip the folder open. Just a peek.
choices.result_text: Sale prices, floor areas, contact numbers. Figures stamped in red catch his eye.

choices.text: Wait for him to come back. Say something.
choices.result_text: {name} sits and waits for the man to come back. His heart beats a little faster.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice. Drink the coffee.
choices.result_text:
He hears it — but that's as far as it goes.
{name} leaves the folder closed and drinks the coffee.
Only a name and a few words stay lodged in the back of the mind.

title: What Was Stolen
description:
The folder opens. Pricing, unit sizes, and a contact —
"Manager Kim 010-XXXX-XXXX." A red stamp: CONFIRMED.
{name} memorizes the number.

Then a shadow falls.
The man returns — and looks back and forth between {name} and the open folder.
"...What exactly are you doing?"

choices.text: Be honest. Apologize. "Sorry — I was just very interested."
choices.result_text: {name} lowers his head. The man is quiet for a moment. An unexpected expression crosses his face.

choices.text: Look away. Act like nothing happened.
choices.result_text:
"Oh, sorry — I thought this was my table."
{name} smiles awkwardly and looks away.
The man gathers the folder with a suspicious look and leaves.

Even after the folder disappears, the number remains in {name}'s head.

title: Caught Honest
description:
{name} bows his head.
"I'm unemployed. I don't have much to my name.
But I want to be here someday — that's why I looked.
I'm sorry."

The man stares for a long moment. Then he lets out a short laugh.
"You're crazy. But that look in your eyes—I had it too, once."

choices.text: "May I ask you just one thing?"
choices.result_text:
The man sets a business card on the table.
"Learn the basics first. Giving an unprepared guy an opportunity is asking for trouble.
When you're actually ready, call. If not, delete the number."

{name} receives the card with both hands, checks the name and number, and slips it into the notebook. The contact comes directly from the man.

title: Speaking Up
description:
The man returns. {name} gathers the nerve.
"Excuse me — what you were talking about just now... I'd like to hear more."

The man sizes {name} up with guarded eyes.
Old puffer jacket. Worn sneakers. An americano gone cold.
"...What do you do?"

choices.text: Honest. "I'm unemployed. I want to learn."
choices.result_text: When {name} finishes, the man's gaze changes. He looks him up and down again.

choices.text: Play it up. "I do a bit of this kind of work myself."
choices.result_text: The man nods, then looks over {name} again as if he has already caught the lie.

title: Lowering the Bar
description:
"Unemployed. But I can't keep living like this —
so I came all the way to Gangnam, bought a coffee, and sat down trying to learn something."

The man laughs incredulously. Then he turns his chair around.
"A guy in an old puffer jacket butts into a 50-million-won conversation.
But fine — you've got time on your hands. Ten minutes. I'll talk for ten minutes."

choices.result_text:
Ten minutes becomes thirty.
Gap investments, leverage, entry rights, premiums —
{name} copies the unfamiliar real-estate terms into the notebook.

The man gives no business card and no name. Even so, the numbers and terms remain on the page.

title: The Bluff
description:
"You work in this field. Is that right?"
The man's eyes narrow. Testing.
"Purchase price: 500 million. Jeonse deposit: 350 million. Loan: 100 million.
Before closing costs, how much cash goes in?"

{name} cannot work it out.
Cold sweat runs down the back.

choices.text: Bluff through it. Throw out a number.
choices.result_text: "About 200 million or so..." {name}'s words tangle. The man seems to catch it at once.

choices.text: Cave. "...I don't actually know. I'm sorry."
choices.result_text: {name} cannot lift his head. But strangely, after a moment, the man smiles.

title: Caught
description:
"Around... 200 million won?" {name} tosses out a random number.
The man scoffs.
"Five hundred minus the 350 million deposit and 100 million loan is 50 million. Kid, do the math before you pretend you know this."

People at nearby tables glance over.
{name}'s face burns. One number is enough to expose the bluff.

choices.result_text:
{name} walks out with the coffee barely touched.
The winter air hits the burning cheeks.
The failed calculation stays in {name}'s head all the way home. The notebook comes out, and {name} subtracts each figure from 500 million again.

title: After Falling
description:
{name}'s head drops.
"...I'm sorry. I don't know any of it.
I was just so desperate — I pretended to know."

The man is quiet for a moment, then lets out a short breath.
"First time I've seen someone admit it that quickly after a bluff.
That's better. Remember one thing.
If you don't know, say so. At least you won't lose money for saying that."

choices.text: Write those words in the notebook.
choices.result_text:
The man leaves without another word.
No business card. No name.
{name} writes one line in the notebook.
'Don't pretend to know a number you don't understand.'

title: The Time of an Americano
description:
{name} ignores the next table and stares at the resume.
Six years of blank. How to fill that gap in words — no idea.

Two hours in. The coffee is long gone.
Then a part-timer quietly approaches and refills the cup.
"...You've been here a while. This one's on the house. It's cold, so I made it hot."
A stranger's small kindness leaves {name} briefly stunned.

choices.result_text:
"...Thank you. Really."
The warmth of the paper cup makes {name}'s eyes sting.

{name} drinks the coffee and fills in the last blank on the résumé. That is enough for the day.

choices.text: Get flustered. Leave without saying much.
choices.result_text:
{name} murmurs a thank-you and gets up.
The warmth of the paper cup lingers in the hand all the way home.
